explained.tdh.spec.s1.title: Scope and conventions
explained.tdh.spec.s1.label: Scope
explained.tdh.spec.s1.heading: What the rules define
explained.tdh.spec.s1.body: TDH v1.4 defines, for one cycle, each wallet's and each identity's balance, raw days, base, boost and final TDH for every eligible token, and the network totals. Arithmetic is exact, with {binary64} only at the ties of RATE and FINAL (§8.1, §8.4), and every number and address comes from the registry (§10). Ranks, xTDH, Rep, upload files and the old Merkle root are out of scope.
explained.tdh.spec.s1.code: The conventions every formula below uses
explained.tdh.spec.s2.title: Inputs and contract registry
explained.tdh.spec.s2.label: Inputs
explained.tdh.spec.s2.heading: Four contracts' logs and one state read
explained.tdh.spec.s2.body: A cycle's inputs are the canonical Ethereum chain up to its cutoff block B, every log of four contracts in blocks up to B, the edition-floor state of a fifth contract read at B, and the registry of the rule version. Prices, Meme Lab, received xTDH, Rep and $6529 balances are not inputs.
explained.tdh.spec.s2.delegationEvents: Register and revoke, direct and through a sub-delegate
explained.tdh.spec.s2.topics: Event signatures and their topic hashes
explained.tdh.spec.s2.topicsCode: The event signatures and their topic hashes
explained.tdh.spec.s3.title: Canonical events
explained.tdh.spec.s3.label: Events
explained.tdh.spec.s3.heading: Every log once, decoded strictly, in one order
explained.tdh.spec.s3-1.title: Log selection
explained.tdh.spec.s3-1.body: Every log of the four contracts in a block up to B is an input, exactly once, the logs the rules ignore included. A node that cannot show it holds them all, from each contract's deployment to B, publishes no result. Two logs at one position, or a later log in a block with a smaller transaction index, make the input invalid.
explained.tdh.spec.s3-2.title: Decoding
explained.tdh.spec.s3-2.body: Three transfer events produce transfers, each decoded byte for byte from its canonical Solidity encoding. Every value has a type and is read at it, none cut to fit; a value outside its type, or a malformed log, makes the input invalid, and a node must not skip it. All transfers of one transaction share one timestamp and one transaction hash.
explained.tdh.spec.s3-3.title: Normalization and order
explained.tdh.spec.s3-3.body: Zero-amount and self transfers move nothing but are kept, because a zero-amount mint is how a card is created. Transfers in different transactions keep on-chain order, even within one block ({dev2}, D121). Within one transaction, each token's movements are netted first (§7.1); the mint facts of §5, the underflow test and the position checks read the transfers before netting.
explained.tdh.spec.s3-4.title: Mints, burns and sinks
explained.tdh.spec.s3-4.body: A mint is a transfer from the zero address to any other address; it debits nobody. A transfer to a sink, the zero address or {dead}, is a burn. Sinks are credit-only: they receive records but are never debited and never consolidated, so a send from {dead} credits its recipient with fresh copies without being a mint. The FirstGM burn transaction is not credited to the zero address, and burns do not reduce editions.
explained.tdh.spec.s4.title: Cycle, cutoff and whole days
explained.tdh.spec.s4.label: Time
explained.tdh.spec.s4.heading: One result per day, from the finalized chain
explained.tdh.spec.s4.body: Cycle N closes at midnight UTC on day N, counted in days since the Unix epoch, and exactly one result exists per cycle (D30). Its cutoff block B is the last block before that moment on the finalized chain, and the cycle has no result until the block after B is finalized. Ages are measured to B's own time, T, as 6529.io measures them ({dev17}).
explained.tdh.spec.s4.code: The cutoff block, its time and whole days
explained.tdh.spec.s4.binds: The result binds (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash). Header timestamps must strictly increase across every header a node reads; a transfer or delegation event stamped after T makes the input invalid.
explained.tdh.spec.s5.title: Eligibility, editions, rates and seasons
explained.tdh.spec.s5.label: Editions and floors
explained.tdh.spec.s5-1.title: Eligibility
explained.tdh.spec.s5-1.body: A Meme or a Gradient counts once its first mint, of any amount, is at least {age} seconds before T; a NextGen token counts once minted. The number of eligible Memes is a count, never the highest id.
explained.tdh.spec.s5-2.title: A Meme's effective edition
explained.tdh.spec.s5-2.code: A Meme's effective edition and H
explained.tdh.spec.s5-2.body: The floor stands for copies the release will still add: below {threshold} minted, a final airdrop tops the edition up to {cap}, above the Nakamoto Threshold of {threshold}. From {threshold} copies on, the minted count is the edition. {totalMax} is the Manifold claim's limit for the card at block B, read with a storage proof; a token with no claim gives zero.
explained.tdh.spec.s5-2.trap: A legacy constant of 6529.io's code. FirstGM minted {minted} copies; its effective edition is {edition}, which makes H = {h}. The adjustment stands for one burn transaction, named in the registry as {burnTx}, and that burn is not credited again to the burn address. Read FirstGM's minted count from the chain without it and every rate comes out wrong.
explained.tdh.spec.s5-3.title: Rates
explained.tdh.spec.s5-3.body: A Meme with an effective edition of zero is eligible but has no rate, and a copy of it makes the input invalid ({dev19}). With no eligible Meme, H is zero: a Gradient gets the minimum and NextGen nothing ({dev18}).
explained.tdh.spec.s5-4.title: Seasons
explained.tdh.spec.s5-4.body: Seasons come from the registry's list of season starts, which must start at the first Meme and strictly increase. The highest season listed for a day is current; a season pays its bonus of {bonus} when it is not current and is no later than season {last}. A new season must be added, as a new rule version, before its first card becomes eligible.
explained.tdh.spec.s6.title: Consolidation
explained.tdh.spec.s6.label: Consolidation
explained.tdh.spec.s6.heading: Up to {max} wallets, linked both ways
explained.tdh.spec.s6-1.title: Events
explained.tdh.spec.s6-1.body: Only delegation events with the consolidation use case, for The Memes or the all-collections address, between two different wallets neither of which is a sink, are kept: a sink is never consolidated. Every event's position is checked, kept or not, and two events at one position make the input invalid. Expiry, all-tokens flags, token ids and update events are ignored.
explained.tdh.spec.s6-2.title: Pair state
explained.tdh.spec.s6-2.body: Each unordered pair of wallets has at most one row. A registration in one direction is pending; the other direction confirms it. Each direction keeps the time of its wallet's latest registration, which the gate below compares. This is 6529.io's own row plan, which D136 adopts; the collection does not partition the state ({dev12}).
explained.tdh.spec.s6-3.title: Clusters
explained.tdh.spec.s6-3.body: Confirmed pairs, newest block first and then by pair key, grow groups in which every pair is confirmed. Up to {ungated} wallets group as before. A group grows past {ungated}, up to {max}, only through a member whose links with all the others were registered both ways at or after {gate}; registrations made before it never form a larger group. This is 6529.io's grouping, which D136 adopts.
explained.tdh.spec.s6-4.title: Effective state and identity key
explained.tdh.spec.s6-4.body: The grouping after every event up to B applies to the whole history of the cycle, transfers made before the wallets were linked included ({dev10}). An identity's key is its sorted lowercase addresses joined by a hyphen; a wallet in no confirmed pair is its own identity.
explained.tdh.spec.s7.title: Holdings
explained.tdh.spec.s7.label: Holdings
explained.tdh.spec.s7.heading: Each copy's time, from netted transfers
explained.tdh.spec.s7-1.title: Acquisition stacks
explained.tdh.spec.s7-1.body: Three steps, in this order: the underflow test over the transfers before netting, transaction netting, and the replay of the netted transfers into each wallet's list of acquisition times. Netting adds up each address's movements of a token within one transaction and pairs the senders with the receivers in address order, so a copy that leaves and comes back in one transaction never left (D131).
explained.tdh.spec.s7-1.underflow: Step one: the underflow test, before netting
explained.tdh.spec.s7-1.replay: Step three: the replay, after netting
explained.tdh.spec.s7-1.property: The stacks depend only on each transaction's net movements. The property stops there: the mint facts of §5 read the steps, so a mint and its burn inside one transaction change no stack but can change editions, rates and other holders' TDH. How sure tells that story.
explained.tdh.spec.s7-1.replayNote: Removal is from the end of the sending wallet's list. After a move inside an identity an old time can be last, and it is then removed first: this is 6529.io's behaviour, and it must be kept.
explained.tdh.spec.s7-2.title: Per-token values
explained.tdh.spec.s7-2.body: For each eligible token a wallet holds: its balance is the number of copies, its raw days the sum of each copy's whole days, and its base the rate times the raw days, rounded. A token that is not eligible contributes nothing, not even balance.
explained.tdh.spec.s7-3.title: Records
explained.tdh.spec.s7-3.body: A wallet has a record when it holds an eligible token or belongs to a group; an identity has one when any of its wallets does. An identity's balance, raw days and base are the sums of its wallets'. Boost and final are computed per record, so an identity's final is not the sum of its wallets' finals.
explained.tdh.spec.s8.title: Arithmetic and scores
explained.tdh.spec.s8.label: Rate
explained.tdh.spec.s8-1.title: A card's rate, in cents
explained.tdh.spec.s8-1.trap: RATE is {halfUpRule} except at an exact half cent, when {oddRule} is an odd integer. Then the {binary64} value of n / d decides. With H = {h} this happens only for editions {editions}: {call} is {rate}, where plain half-up gives {halfUp}. Use two {binary64} roundings, no fused multiply-add.
explained.tdh.spec.s8-3.title: Boost
explained.tdh.spec.s8-3.body: A record holds a token when the token is eligible and its balance is positive, whatever the copies' ages. The extra-set bonus grows towards a limit and stops once its rounded value reaches it; a program derives that point from the registry and must not hard-code it. The cent rounding of the boost never meets a tie.
explained.tdh.spec.s8-4.title: Final, totals and range
explained.tdh.spec.s8-4.body: FINAL is computed per token, and a record's final is their sum. The total is the sum of identity finals, never of wallet finals; a second total leaves out the burn addresses, which never enter any consensus weight ({dev13}). A cycle whose values leave the range where {binary64} is exact has no result, and inside it the hardware and exact evaluations agree.
explained.tdh.spec.s9.title: Cycle output and roots
explained.tdh.spec.s9.label: Output and roots
explained.tdh.spec.s9.heading: What a day's result is
explained.tdh.spec.s9.body: A cycle result is its header, (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash), and each identity's key, wallets, boost and final TDH. Each token carries its balance, raw, base and final. Validators commit to it with a cycle root and a wallet root. How a result is serialized and hashed into them belongs to P28 and P11, which are not public yet. A separate implementation can match every final TDH and the totals today, not the roots.
explained.tdh.spec.s9.receipt: The day's receipt prints both roots for every published day: {link}.
explained.tdh.spec.s10.title: The parameter registry
explained.tdh.spec.s10.label: The registry
explained.tdh.spec.s10.heading: Every parameter, read, never hard-coded
explained.tdh.spec.s10.table: The parameters of the TDH v1.4 registry
explained.tdh.spec.s10.used.age: §5.1 a card counts a day after its first mint
explained.tdh.spec.s10.note: Boosts are stored in micro-units and rates in cents; lists are strictly ascending. The full record, with every field's type and the encoding that hashes to {registry}, is vector {vector}.

explained.tdh.spec.s11.body: Each place where TDH v1.4 departs from the code 6529.io ran removes a dependency on mutable data, database order, timing or floating point; none changes the formula. Effects were measured on the replay of {day}. {settled} is settled and no longer a deviation.

explained.tdh.spec.dev.DEV-5.v14: The first mint of any amount starts the clock

explained.tdh.spec.dev.DEV-8.v14: A versioned list of season starts
explained.tdh.spec.dev.DEV-9.old: Consolidations read when the job runs, recomputed during the day

explained.tdh.spec.dev.DEV-11.v14: By ascending pair key, as 6529.io now orders them

explained.tdh.spec.dev.DEV-13.v14: Records kept; totals also given without them

explained.tdh.spec.dev.DEV-22.v14: Not kept: a burn address is never consolidated

explained.tdh.spec.s12.body: What TDH v1.4 does about each: most are removed; the carry over history and the link state are kept by decision, and the upload files are outside the rules.

explained.tdh.spec.s13.title: Conformance
explained.tdh.spec.s13.label: Conformance
explained.tdh.spec.s13.heading: What conformance means
explained.tdh.spec.s13.body: An implementation conforms when it reproduces every vector and, for a real day, the reference implementation's output from the same canonical input. Until the vectors and the input files are published, an outside implementation can conform to the {count} public vectors and hit the published roots; the {link} says how.
explained.tdh.spec.s13.invalid: A vector that expects no result passes when its input is rejected, for any reason: P26 sets no precedence among the rules that make an input invalid. A file that is not a vector at all, not JSON or a member named twice, fails every implementation.
explained.tdh.spec.evidence.title: Checked against a real day
explained.tdh.spec.evidence.body: Replayed on {day}, TDH v1.4 with netting reproduces every live identity and wallet. From raw logs read by the validator's own ingestion, the Python reference gives the live total, {total} ({withoutBurn} without the burn addresses), and every live record, and the second implementation agrees on every record. The four-wallet rule changes nothing on that day: its cutoff is before the gate opened.
